overview: Long Rock is the middle of the long, open beach that sweeps around Mount’s Bay for about three miles from Penzance to Marazion, named after a tidal rock just offshore. The coast path and the main railway line run along the sea wall behind it.
It’s a big, airy beach with views of St Michael’s Mount all the way along, and plenty of space even in summer.

expect.title: The walk to Marazion
expect.text: Follow the coast path or the sand east towards Marazion and St Michael’s Mount, with the Mount in view the whole way.

expect.title: Marazion Marsh
expect.text: An RSPB nature reserve sits just inland near Marazion, good for birdwatching.

goodToKnow.label: Where it is
goodToKnow.text: About a mile east of Penzance and a mile west of Marazion.

goodToKnow.label: Village
goodToKnow.text: Long Rock village has a shop and two pubs.

week.text: A good spot for a long beach walk in Mount’s Bay, especially if you’re staying in Penzance. It faces south, so it’s a good alternative when the north coast is rough.

pairWith.why: the beach for the causeway to St Michael’s Mount
the island castle across the bay
art in a valley garden just inland

tips: Walk the coast path between Penzance and Marazion for a flat, easy few miles with the Mount ahead of you.
